text: More than 5,000 years ago, the people of Crete, the largest Greek island, began working copper and bronze.
About 3,900 years ago they built the first palaces in Europe, at Knossos, Phaistos and Malia.
src: Crete, the largest of the Greek islands / Around 3100 BCE, as copper and then bronze working spread, the island entered the Early Minoan period
From about 1900 BCE the people of Bronze Age Crete built Europe’s first palaces, at Knossos, Phaistos and Malia

text: Each palace had a long central court, with storerooms, workshops and shrines all around it.
Huge clay jars stored oil, wine and grain, and stone drains carried water away.
src: Each was built around a long rectangular central court, surrounded by storerooms, workshops, shrines and halls
great clay storage jars, pithoi, for oil, wine and grain / stone drains and terracotta pipes carried water and waste

text: Paintings show young athletes leaping over charging bulls, perhaps as a sport, a ritual or both.
People worshipped on mountain tops and in caves, leaving little clay figures, perhaps as offerings.
src: Bull-leaping, shown in wall paintings, on seals and in bronze, in which young athletes grasp or vault over a charging bull, may have been a ritual, a sport or both
Peak sanctuaries on mountain tops / have yielded many clay figurines of people and animals and models of limbs, perhaps offered in hope of healing / Caves were sacred too

text: Potters made cups and jars with walls as thin as eggshell, painted white, red and orange on a dark background.
Later pots were painted with octopuses, lilies and seaweed.
src: vessels with walls sometimes as thin as eggshell, painted in white, red and orange on a dark ground
with lilies and grasses and, in the Marine Style, octopuses, argonauts and seaweed spread over the whole vessel

text: Their ships carried trade to Egypt, Cyprus and other lands of the eastern Mediterranean.
Rulers in mainland Greece wanted Cretan goods and skills, like the gold cups found at Vapheio.
src: their ships carried their trade to Egypt, Cyprus and the Levant / the eastern Mediterranean
The elites rising on the Greek mainland eagerly acquired Cretan goods and skills, as the Minoan-style metalwork of the shaft graves of Mycenae and the gold cups from Vapheio show

text: More than 3,400 years ago, fires destroyed many palaces, and Greeks from the mainland ruled from Knossos.
Later Greeks told myths of King Minos and his Labyrinth, and Minoan writing, Linear A, still cannot be read.
src: Around 1450 BCE fires destroyed the palaces of Phaistos, Malia and Zakros / after about 1450 BCE Mycenaean Greeks ruled from Knossos
The Greeks remembered Bronze Age Crete in myth: Minos the lawgiver king, the Labyrinth built by Daedalus / Their Linear A script is still undeciphered
